Extract values from netCDF files at point observations

Source: R/extract_to_points.R
extract_to_point.Rd

A convenience wrapper over the build and intersect steps: it turns the observations into SpatVector3D points with as_vector3d(), describes the netCDF data with as_proxy(), and reads the value at every point with extract(), which reads each time step once for all the points in it. The same can be done step by step; see the workflow article, vignette("workflow-values-in-shapes").

Usage

extract_to_point(
  data = NULL,
  nc,
  lon = NULL,
  lat = NULL,
  depth = NULL,
  date = NULL,
  var = NULL,
  method = c("2d", "surface", "bottom", "nearest"),
  lon_col = "lon",
  lat_col = "lat",
  date_col = "date",
  depth_col = "depth",
  id_col = NULL,
  lon_dim = NULL,
  lat_dim = NULL,
  depth_dim = NULL,
  time_dim = NULL,
  time_match = c("nearest", "exact"),
  max_time_diff = NULL,
  output_prefix = NULL,
  output_col = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Optional observations: a data frame, tibble, sf object with POINT geometries, numeric matrix with column names, or named list. If NULL, give the coordinates directly with lon, lat, and depth and date as needed. sf points need a CRS and are transformed to longitude and latitude.

nc

The netCDF data: a file path, several paths for a series of files on one grid (each with its own time steps, such as one file per day), a connection opened with ncdf4::nc_open(), or a SpatProxy from as_proxy(). Paths and connections are read through as_proxy(); a SpatProxy is used as it is, so var and the dimension arguments don't apply to it.

lon, lat, depth, date

Direct input when data = NULL: numeric longitudes, latitudes and depths (metres, positive down), and dates or date-times. Each has length 1 or the same length as the others. depth is needed for method = "nearest".

var

Name of the variable. NULL detects it when the file holds one data variable.

method

"2d" (default) for a variable without depth or with a single depth level, or "surface", "bottom" or "nearest" for one with depth levels (see Details).

lon_col, lat_col, date_col, depth_col

Columns of data with the longitude, latitude, date and depth. date_col is needed when the variable has dated time steps (not a climatology); depth_col for method = "nearest". The coordinate columns must be numeric.

id_col

Optional column of observation identifiers. It is checked to exist; extraction doesn't use it.

lon_dim, lat_dim, depth_dim, time_dim

Optional dimension names, passed to as_proxy().

time_match

"nearest" (default) or "exact": how observation times are matched to time steps, as in as_voxel().

max_time_diff

Optional largest gap, in days, between an observation and its nearest time step with time_match = "nearest"; NULL (default) allows any gap.

output_col, output_prefix

Name of the output column. If both are given, output_col is used. By default, the variable's name, or with var detected, surface_<var>, seabottom_<var> or nearest_<var> for those methods.

Value

With data, the observations with the value column added. Data frames, tibbles and sf objects keep their class; matrices and named lists become data frames. With direct input, a numeric vector, one value per point. A value is NA when the observation lies off the grid, has no coordinates, has no time step within max_time_diff, or has no level its method can take.

Details

You choose the depth level with method, which follows the rules of the same name in extract(): "nearest" takes the level nearest the observation's depth, skipping levels without a value; "surface" takes the shallowest level, even if it has no value; "bottom" takes the deepest level with a value. "2d" is for a variable without depth. Each observation takes the cell that contains it. Times are matched to the nearest time step by default (see time_match and max_time_diff): a date by its UTC day, a date-time as an instant.

See also

extract() for the step this wraps; extract_to_buffer() and extract_to_track().

Examples

nc_file <- system.file("extdata", "example_3d.nc", package = "ocean3d")

# One observation: the nearest level with a value, on 3 January.
extract_to_point(nc = nc_file, lon = 0, lat = 40, depth = 60,
                 date = "2020-01-03", var = "temp", method = "nearest")
#> [1] 15.5

# A table of observations keeps its columns and gains one.
obs <- data.frame(id = c("a", "b"), lon = c(0, 1), lat = c(40, 41),
                  depth = c(60, 100),
                  date = as.Date(c("2020-01-03", "2020-01-03")))
extract_to_point(obs, nc_file, var = "temp", method = "bottom")
#>   id lon lat depth       date temp
#> 1  a   0  40    60 2020-01-03 10.5
#> 2  b   1  41   100 2020-01-03 13.5
